alternate_mechanisms.name: fear_reversed_from_subject_to_audience
alternate_mechanisms.summary: لَا blocks fear from entering the sovereign subject, but the narrated punitive aftermath sends fear outward toward accountable hearers. The clause therefore performs warning through the very affect it denies of its grammatical subject.

alternate_mechanisms.name: causal_consequence_without_causal_blowback
alternate_mechanisms.summary: The judgment genuinely has a sequel and produces effects, but no counter-effect can return upon its author as harm or liability. The negation distinguishes consequence from blowback: outcomes follow the act, while adverse accountability does not ascend beyond the final judge.

alternate_mechanisms.name: offense_to_sentence_to_nonreviewable_closure
alternate_mechanisms.summary: The preceding sin grounds punitive consequence; possible pursuit, review, reversal, or compensatory claim then defines the ordinary aftermath of judgment. Divine non-fear closes every such route, yielding finality without implying that justice is ungrounded or arbitrary.

alternate_mechanisms.name: destruction_divides_into_removal_and_surviving_trace
alternate_mechanisms.summary: The preceding punishment removes and levels, yet its aftermath leaves a trace that survives in collective memory and recitation. Physical diminution and historical remainder are complementary sides of the same act, and the surviving trace becomes the warning projected to later hearers.
